subject: Finova — Performance SLO / Multi-region routing (post-call follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finova.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@finova.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Finova - Post-call recap & SLO questions

Hi Alex / Elena,

Thanks for the great call today — appreciate the time and detail. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can size and propose a dedicated configuration that matches your production SLOs.

Recap (from our discussion):
- Primary workload: interactive chat + summary generation for banking customer support (mix of short Q&A and longer summarizations).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~500 req/s (text-gen requests) across the platform; peak bursts up to ~2k req/s during 2x daily spikes.
- Typical prompt size: 1.5k tokens input, expected completion 200–800 tokens depending on the prompt.
- Regions: US (primary), EU (GDPR/data residency), APAC (SG/Japan for latency-sensitive APAC customers).
- Current latency targets: 95th percentile target around 200ms for US, 250ms EU, 350ms APAC (TBD). Streaming of partial outputs is required for UX.
- Data residency: EU customer data must stay within EU; APAC may require Singapore-based residency for regulatory customers.

Follow-ups / asks from our side so engineering can size correctly: 
1) Can you confirm the 95p latency targets for each region (US/EU/APAC) and whether 200ms (US) is a hard SLA or a target for planning?
2) For throughput — is the ~500 req/s steady-state per region or global? How frequently do bursts happen and what concurrency profile should we expect (e.g., many concurrent sessions vs fewer high-throughput streams)?
3) Streaming requirements — do you need server-sent-events / chunked HTTP streaming for all responses, or only for the longer completion paths? Any OAuth/token refresh requirements for streaming sessions?
4) Data residency — are EU requests strictly bound to EU-based endpoints, or is pseudonymization/field-level redaction an option to allow routing through US infrastructure?

Next steps we propose:
- Nikhil (cc'ed) to draft a load-test plan and candidate SLO configurations for each region.
- If you can share a sample payload (anonymized prompts + expected completion sizes), we can run a three-hour smoke test in a staging environment and share latency percentiles.
- Align on procurement timeline so we can provision Dedicated capacity in the desired regions.

Attaching a short template for the payloads and an outline of the load-test approach.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: payload-sample-template.json (see Drive link)
From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@finova.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finova - Post-call recap & SLO questions

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Quick answers below: 

1) Latency: the 95p numbers I quoted are our target for a good UX. For contractual SLAs we can negotiate, but for sizing please treat 200ms (US), 250ms (EU), 350ms (APAC) as the goals we want to meet under normal production load.
2) Throughput: the ~500 req/s is global steady-state, but we expect roughly 60% in US, 30% EU, 10% APAC. Bursts happen twice a day for ~20–40 minutes where global traffic can spike 3–4x. Concurrency tends to be many concurrent sessions (hundreds to low thousands) with streaming enabled.
3) Streaming: yes — chunked HTTP streaming (SSE or chunked responses) is required for the chat UX. Token TTLs and refresh are standard OAuth2 flows. We will handle auth tokens from our side.
4) Data residency: EU data must remain in EU endpoints. Pseudonymization is possible for lower-risk flows, but core customer PII must not leave EU.

I'll loop in Procurement once we have a rough config and runbook for provisioning. Attaching the SOC2 questionnaire Elena mentioned.

—Alex
Alex Porter | Head of Engineering, Finova
alex.porter@finova.com

Attachment: finova-soc2-questionnaire.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finova.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@finova.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finova - Post-call recap & SLO questions

Perfect — thanks Alex.

Nikhil / Aditya,
Couple of technical clarifications for sizing:
- The 500 req/s global with 3–4x bursts implies we should propose Dedicated pools per region with burst-able capacity (or cross-region failover). Which approach do you think is better for predictable latency under bursts?
- For streaming, we need to know expected mean completion size. Alex — you mentioned 200–800 tokens; can you confirm distribution (e.g., 60% short <300 tokens, 30% medium 300–600, 10% long >600)?
- Also: what concurrency do we expect per user session? Do streams keep a persistent connection for the duration of the completion (i.e., long-lived HTTP connections)?

Alex — if you can drop a quick sample of 10 anonymized prompts and size distribution (or confirm the percentages), we'll plug that into the load plan.

I'll ask Nikhil to sketch a two-option configuration: 1) Dedicated per region sized to meet 95p targets with regional autoscale; 2) Hybrid routing with US primary and EU-resident compute only for EU PII (pseudonymized fallback otherwise).

Cheers,
Marissa
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Alex Porter <alex.porter@finova.com>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@finova.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Load-test plan + technical notes for Finova (draft)

Hi all — following up with a draft plan and a few notes. Attaching a short PDF with the load-test windows and ops checklist.

Key technical assumptions (please confirm):
- Model: customer will run ~Redwood-Open-3B quantized variant for most traffic; larger variants for heavy summarization (we'll map those to separate pools).
- Input distribution: 60% short (<300 tokens), 30% medium (300–600), 10% long (>600).
- Steady-state: global 500 req/s (US 60% / EU 30% / APAC 10%). Peak: up to 2k req/s sustained for 20–40 minutes during bursts.
- Concurrency: average active connections ~1.2x requests/sec per second; long-lived streaming connections will last the duration of the completion (~1–10s typical, up to 30s for long tails).

Sizing notes: 
- For 95p = 200ms (US) for median-level prompts we recommend a Dedicated pool in US-West with continuous batching and auto-scaling to handle 2k burst. We'll also enable prefix KV caching for common prompts to reduce per-token work.
- EU: separate Dedicated pool in eu-west with data residency enforced (no cross-region KV or logging). Aim for warm standby capacity to avoid cold-start latency.
- APAC: recommend Singapore (asia-southeast1) with smaller Dedicated nodes; because target latency is higher, we can use smaller GPU instances but keep streaming enabled.

Streaming: we support chunked HTTP streaming (event-streams) with per-connection KV cache. For long-lived connections we expose a keepalive heartbeat. We can support both SSE and chunked transfer; we'll align on whichever your frontend prefers.

Throughput testing plan (three-phased):
1) Smoke (1 hour): validate correctness and basic latency under 100 req/s per region.
2) Ramp (3 hours): ramp to steady-state 500 req/s global with regional split. Monitor 50/95/99 latencies, GPU utilization, and queue depth.
3) Burst (1 hour): simulate 3–4x spikes (1.5k–2k req/s) and validate 95p targets and autoscale response.

Data residency / logging: for EU-resident flows we will ensure compute + logs remain in eu-west; cross-region analytics will be pseudonymized. We will provide an SOC2 attestation and can support field-level redaction if needed.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex / Elena: confirm payload sample and the token distribution above.
- Finova: sign off on two-hour window for the ramp test (we recommend 2027-05-12 02:00–06:00 UTC to minimize user impact).
- Procurement: we'll prepare a capacity proposal and preliminary pricing for Dedicated pools per region.

Attachment: redwood-load-test-plan.pdf

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
